git.gitignore_content:
# Framework (Privacy-First Mode)
# ================================================================================
# This project uses Framework's privacy-first structure.
# All */private/ directories are gitignored by default.
#
# WORKFLOW:
#   1. Protected data goes in */private/ directories (NEVER committed)
#   2. Reviewed metadata goes in inputs/metadata/ (ignored; agents can read it)
#   3. Simulated data goes in inputs/simulated/ (ignored; agents can read it)
#   4. Analysis scripts are committed, but outputs are carefully controlled
#
# CRITICAL: Private directories are NEVER committed to version control.
# ================================================================================

# ============================================================================
# SENSITIVE DATA - NEVER COMMIT
# ============================================================================

# Private directories - explicit paths for this project type
/inputs/private/
/reference/private/
/outputs/private/

# Generic private directory patterns (defense-in-depth)
**/private/**
**/*_private/**
**/sensitive/**

# Allow structure documentation (README and .gitkeep files in private dirs)
!/inputs/**/README.md
!/inputs/**/.gitkeep
!/reference/**/README.md
!/reference/**/.gitkeep
!/outputs/**/README.md
!/outputs/**/.gitkeep

# Reviewed metadata and simulated data. Agents can read these folders, but
# their contents still derive from protected data, so git ignores them.
# The negations keep the empty folders (via .gitkeep) in the repository.
/inputs/metadata/**
/inputs/simulated/**
!/inputs/metadata/**/
!/inputs/simulated/**/
!/inputs/metadata/**/.gitkeep
!/inputs/simulated/**/.gitkeep

# ============================================================================
# SECRETS AND CREDENTIALS - NEVER COMMIT
# ============================================================================

.env
.env.local
.env.*.local
.Renviron
.httr-oauth
**/credentials/**
**/secrets/**
*.key
*.pem
*.p12
*.pfx

# ============================================================================
# UTILITY & CACHE - SAFE TO IGNORE
# ============================================================================

# Temporary processing directories
**/cache/**
**/scratch/**
**/tmp/**
**/temp/**

# Logs (run logs, cluster job output)
**/logs/**
slurm-*.out

# ============================================================================
# R ENVIRONMENT
# ============================================================================

# R session files
.Rproj.user/
.Rhistory
.RData
.Ruserdata
.Rapp.history
.Rprofile

# renv (package management)
# NOTE: Consider committing renv.lock for reproducibility
renv/library/
renv/local/
renv/cellar/
renv/lock/
renv/python/
renv/sandbox/
renv/staging/

# ============================================================================
# FRAMEWORK INTERNALS
# ============================================================================

framework.db
framework.db-wal
framework.db-shm
.initiated
.framework_renv_enabled
.framework_scaffolded

# ============================================================================
# QUARTO / RMARKDOWN ARTIFACTS
# ============================================================================

# Quarto adds these two lines, in this form, unless they are here already
/.quarto/
**/*.quarto_ipynb
# A folder with its own _quarto.yml gets its own .quarto/
.quarto/
_freeze/
# Backups from quarto_regenerate() before Framework 2.0.1
.quarto_backups/
*_cache/
*_files/

# ============================================================================
# PYTHON (if using reticulate)
# ============================================================================

__pycache__/
.ipynb_checkpoints/
*.pyc
.pytest_cache/
venv/
.venv/

# ============================================================================
# IDE & SYSTEM FILES
# ============================================================================

# IDE - personal settings only (commit workspace settings if desired)
.idea/
.vscode/.history/
.positron/.history/
.history/

# macOS
.DS_Store
.AppleDouble
.LSOverride

# Windows
Thumbs.db
ehthumbs.db

# Linux
*~

# ============================================================================
# CLOUD/AWS CONFIG
# ============================================================================

.aws/
.config/

# ============================================================================
# TEMPORARY FILES
# ============================================================================

*.tmp
*.log
*.bak
*.swp
*~

# --- from base framework/project_sensitive v4 ---
# Private data and credentials
**/private/**
**/*_private/**
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
.Renviron
**/credentials/**
**/secrets/**

# Local records and caches
framework.db
framework.db-wal
framework.db-shm
.DS_Store

# Sensitive project folders
/inputs/private/
/reference/private/
/outputs/private/
**/sensitive/**

protected-data.content:
---
name: protected-data
description: Rules for working in a project that holds protected data. Use at the start of every task in this project, and before reading, listing, or searching any file.
---

# Protected data

This project keeps protected data in `private` folders. You develop code on **simulated** data in `inputs/simulated/`, generated from reviewed metadata in `inputs/metadata/`.

## Never

- Read, list, open, search, or run code on anything in `inputs/private/` or `outputs/private/`.
- Ask the user to paste real data, real output, or real summary values into the chat.
- Hard-code values copied from real data into code or text.
- Change a notebook's `data_dir` setting to `"private"`. Only a person does that, without AI.
- Write to `inputs/private/`, even to test `scripts/generate-sim-data.R`. Test it with an output path in a temporary folder.

## Always

- Work only with `inputs/simulated/` and `inputs/metadata/`. Git ignores both folders, so open their files by path.
- Build paths with `here::here()` and the notebook's `data_dir` variable, so a person can switch to the real data by changing one line.
- Treat results as fake. Check that the code runs. Don't interpret the numbers.
- If a task seems to need the real data, **stop and say so** instead of finding a workaround.

## Rendering

Don't run `quarto render` in this project. It writes to `outputs/private/`. Never pass `--output-dir`. To check code, run it with `knitr::knit()` into a temporary folder. The user renders.

```r
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(tempdir(), "figure/"))
knitr::knit("notebooks/01_data-summary.qmd", output = file.path(tempdir(), "01_data-summary.md"))
```
